newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EU de Silguy repeats EMU start should be respected.
newsitem.headline: EU de Silguy repeats EMU start should be respected.

text.p: EU Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy, responsible for economic, financial and monetary affairs, repeated on Friday that the planned start of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 should be respected.
"The year 1999 should be respected as a starting date," de Silguy told a news conference.
De Silguy added that there was strong political consensus in Europe about EMU starting according to plan, which would be on January 1, 1999. "The political commitment is very strong," he said.
De Silguy also repeated that no country could be forced to join EMU, although the EU treaty states that a member country should join EMU when it meets covergence criteria.
"The EU treaty says that a country should join EMU when it meets convergence criteria," de Silguy said. "Here are two important exceptions, Britain and Denmark.
"Regarding such an important decision, I do not know how we will be able to force a country to join EMU if the government does not want to join, and we say it has to join."
He added he found it natural for a country meeting criteria to willingly join.
Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink approved of de Silguy's statement as it coincides with Sweden's minority Social Democratic government's opinion.

"Naturally, it is good that he states this clearly," Asbrink said. "I am very satisfied with this. As we previously have said, it is the political process in a country that decides if the country should join EMU."
Sweden's government has said a Social Democratic party congress will make a decision about EMU membership in the autumn of 1997, which is expected to be followed by a parliamentary vote.
